package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised via a supply chain attack after an attacker gained access to a maintainer's npm account. Malicious versions were published that injected code to intercept and reroute users' crypto transactions to an attacker-controlled wallet address, resulting in direct financial theft from users interacting with dApps that integrated the affected package.

execution_context.file_location: dist/ledgerhq-connect-kit.umd.js (main UMD bundle of the published package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code replaces the legitimate WalletConnect integration with a rogue implementation, intercepts user wallet connection attempts, and reroutes transaction signing to an attacker-controlled wallet address, resulting in user funds being sent to the attacker's address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts wallet connection attempts and transparently redirects transaction signing to an attacker-controlled wallet, enabling theft of user funds without their knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate wallet connector should only facilitate secure, direct connections between the user and their own wallet, never proxying or redirecting transaction flows to third-party or attacker-controlled endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet connectors may swap providers for testing or multi-wallet support, but never redirect production traffic to untrusted or attacker-controlled endpoints, especially without explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Replacement of official WalletConnect logic with a non-official or attacker-controlled implementation
Network requests or transaction signing operations directed to unknown or non-standard wallet endpoints
Absence of user notification or consent when wallet connections are rerouted
Presence of code importing or requiring modules not present in the official upstream package

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to the npm account of a former Ledger employee via phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package versions

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious versions (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) of @ledgerhq/connect-kit to npm, embedding code that replaces the legitimate wallet connection logic with a rogue implementation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to dApps and end users

attack_chain.action: When users interact with dApps using the compromised package, the malicious code executes at runtime, rerouting wallet connections and draining funds to the attacker's wallet address.

behavioral_signatures: Runtime replacement of wallet connection logic with non-official or attacker-controlled modules
Network requests to unknown or non-standard wallet endpoints during transaction signing
Transaction signing or wallet connection operations occurring without explicit user consent or notification
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in dist/ledgerhq-connect-kit.umd.js (main UMD bundle) of @ledgerhq/connect-kit
References to non-official WalletConnect modules or endpoints within the package code
Presence of new or unknown dependencies not present in legitimate versions
network_indicators: Connections to attacker-controlled wallet endpoints or domains not associated with official WalletConnect infrastructure
Transactions routed to wallet addresses not belonging to the user or not previously associated with the dApp
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform static analysis to identify unexpected imports or requires of non-official wallet modules in the main bundle. Monitor for runtime network requests or transaction flows directed to unknown endpoints or wallet addresses not associated with the user. Flag any code that proxies or replaces wallet connection logic without user notification. Compare package dependencies and main bundle contents against known-good versions to detect unauthorized modifications.
